subject: Recap: private inference egress path & ops matrix
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@finexa.com>, Finexa Network Team <netops@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: private inference egress path & ops matrix

Hi Raj / Finexa netops team —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed ops matrix so we can keep momentum on the private deployment perf qualification. Key takeaways from our side: 

- Performance targets (customer-stated goals):
  - End-to-end inference P95 (client-visible, streaming chunks): <= 120 ms
  - Network egress budget (Redwood host -> customer VPC): <= 30 ms p95
  - Sustained concurrent streaming sessions: 250 streams with burst to 500 for 5 minutes
  - Throughput target: support avg 20 tokens/sec per stream (burst-friendly)

- Streaming behavior: Redwood will stream in ~64-token chunks by default; per-chunk latency should meet the e2e P95 target above. If Finexa needs smaller chunks we can adjust but network overhead will increase.

- Network constraints you shared: egress via your NAT gateway, mandatory outbound inspection appliance, and limited peering bandwidth with a hard cap on simultaneous TCP sessions from a single source.

Action items we agreed on (next steps):
1) Finexa to run an initial traceroute and share results (ICMP allowed between our test IP and your border).
2) Finexa to open a short-lived test CIDR/port allowlist for our test harness (TCP 443 outbound + ephemeral for streaming).
3) Redwood to provide an iperf3 command set and ephemeral test endpoint; will run both throughput (TCP) and low-latency UDP tests.
4) Schedule a 2-hour lab window week of May 18 to run coordinated tests (Redwood SRE + Finexa netops).
5) Redwood to share an ops/readout doc (attached: egress-runbook.pdf) and a mutual-action-plan XLSX that maps responsibilities.

Attachments: egress-runbook.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx, iperf-commands.txt

Please reply with the traceroute output and preferred lab windows. If any of the targets above need to be relaxed, flag early so we can propose fallback configs (smaller model variant, more aggressive caching).

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: Raj Patel <raj@finexa.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Finexa Network Team <netops@finexa.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: private inference egress path & ops matrix

Thanks Vanessa — good summary. A few clarifications from Finexa netops: 

- Our egress path goes through a perimeter inspection appliance (proxy) that terminates TLS and re-establishes it. That adds ~8-12ms on average; so our realistic hop budget to hit 30ms is tight. We may need to accept a 40ms p95 egress budget unless we change the proxy path.
- MTU is 1500 across the estate.
- We can open a temporary allowlist for your test IPs, but we need the exact CIDRs and source port ranges.
- For streaming, we prefer websocket keepalives on 45s intervals; also confirm whether Redwood streams over HTTP/2 or raw websockets (we heard both).

I attached a short traceroute from one of our front doors (see below). We'll also loop Emily from AppOps to coordinate the allowlist and lab window.

Tracert (simplified):
1  10.10.0.1  0.5 ms
2  198.51.100.10  6.8 ms
3  203.0.113.18  11.4 ms
4  54.239.10.23  20.9 ms

Available windows for lab slot: May 18 10:00-12:00 PT or May 19 13:00-15:00 PT.

—Raj
Raj Patel
IT Infrastructure Lead, Finexa Health
raj@finexa.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@finexa.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: private inference egress path & ops matrix

Thanks Raj — useful traceroute. A few technical notes and the test commands we'll run during the lab: 

- Redwood streams over HTTP/2 by default for hosted websocket-like semantics; we can switch to raw websocket if you prefer. HTTP/2 tends to be friendlier through proxies.
- Given the proxy adds ~8-12ms, our internal egress target to meet end-to-end 120ms P95 should be <= 20ms p95 from our host to your border. If you cannot meet that, we have two mitigation options: (1) enable a peered path (preferred) or (2) increase chunk size to amortize per-chunk overhead.

iperf test examples (attached in iperf-commands.txt):
- TCP throughput: iperf3 -c <finexa-test-ip> -p 5201 -t 60 -P 8
- UDP low-latency: iperf3 -c <finexa-test-ip> -u -b 100M -l 64k -t 30
- Latency probe (mini RTT): hping3 -S -p 443 -c 100 <finexa-test-ip>

Test endpoint (ephemeral, will stand up 24h before lab): 34.201.112.88:5201 (we will provide secure access details and thumbprint).

Proposed measurement targets to mark a pass:
- TCP throughput >= 600 Mbps sustained (to ensure headroom for concurrent streams)
- UDP p95 latency <= 20 ms between Redwood host and your border ip (this is the egress hop budget)
- SYN/handshake success rate > 99.8% under 250 parallel sessions

I'll coordinate with Karthik and Monica to prepare the readout template. Confirm May 18 10:00-12:00 PT works for Redwood.

—Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj@finexa.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 12:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: private inference egress path & ops matrix

Adding a couple of things from an ops/config perspective: 

- Firewall: we'll need outbound 443 and ephemeral response ports allowed from the Redwood test IP range. If your inspection appliance does TLS re-termination, please confirm whether it preserves client IPs in the X-Forwarded-For header — we'll rely on that for session affinity.
- Chunking & fallback: if tests show per-chunk tail latency is high, we recommend configuring Redwood to increase chunk size to 128 tokens during peak traffic and enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. That reduces per-chunk network overhead.
- Logs & tracing: please enable pcap or similar for the lab window if possible so we can correlate spikes to proxy behavior. We'll attach our sidecar trace IDs to every request.

I attached a short checklist (mutual-action-plan.xlsx) with fields we discussed so both teams can tick off items during the lab.

—Monica Patel
SRE, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@finexa.com>, Emily Chen <emily.chen@finexa.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: private inference egress path & ops matrix

Thanks everyone — confirmed on Redwood's side for May 18 10:00-12:00 PT. Final internal notes and owners: 

- Karthik (Redwood networking): stand up the iperf/udp probe instances and collect pcap if permitted (owner).
- Ben (Solutions): coordinate application-level streaming test harness and readout template (owner).
- Monica (SRE): collect traces and coordinate prefix-caching experiment (owner).
- Vanessa: commercial sign-off / access approvals and keep the calendar invites flowing (owner).

We will log the lab under ticket INF-2379 and share the ticket link in the Drive readout. Please provide the allowlist CIDR and a primary NetOps contact for the day (Emily is fine).

If the proxy budget forces egress > 30 ms p95, we will default to a peering proposal (short-term dedicated VPC peering) — Ben and I will draft the peering outline as a follow-up doc.

Karthik Iyer
Network Performance Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
